question: Why do young women in cities struggle to find work?

brief.question: Why do young women in cities struggle to find work?
brief.answer: In 2025, only 23.2% of urban women aged 15‑29 were in the labour force, far below the overall female LFPR of 40%, indicating limited participation. Moreover, the September 2026 monthly data show that urban women of the same age group faced an unemployment rate of 26.6, compared with just 5.2 for all women, highlighting a much higher difficulty in securing jobs.

PROFILE labour force participation rate (LFPR), annual, 2025, usual status (PS+SS), ages 15+ unless stated
headline (All India, everyone): 59.3%
on the other measure, current weekly status (CWS): 55.7% -- never mix the two
previous year (2024): 59.6%
largest gaps from the total:
  - gender = male: 79.1% vs 59.3% overall (+19.8 points)
  - gender = female: 40% vs 59.3% overall (-19.3 points)
  - education = 6.diploma/ certificate course: 78.6% vs 59.3% overall (+19.3 points)
gaps that change most across another field:
  - The gap women minus men (-39.1 points overall) varies across state: from -58.4 (Delhi) to -9.9 (Ladakh)
  - The gap youth (15-29) minus all 15+ (-13.3 points overall) varies across state: from -27.5 (Mizoram) to +3.5 (Goa); set apart as outliers (possibly small, noisy samples): Ladakh -34.2
  - The gap urban minus rural (-10.6 points overall) varies across state: from -23.5 (Sikkim) to +2.2 (Goa); set apart as outliers (possibly small, noisy samples): Chandigarh +56.1
strongest correlations across states:
  - LFPR female and LFPR male: r = 0.41 over 36 states
  - LFPR urban and LFPR rural: r = 0.38 over 36 states -- rank correlation 0.67 disagrees; driven by Chandigarh
  - LFPR and UR: r = -0.15 over 36 states
biggest changes since last release:
  - state = Andaman & Nicobar Islands: +6.5 points since 2024
  - state = Ladakh: +6.1 points since 2024
  - state = Uttarakhand: -5.6 points since 2024
not findings (true by definition): LFPR 15-29 years vs LFPR 15 years and above r = 0.66, because the age bands overlap (15-29 years, 15 years and above); LFPR vs WPR r = 0.99, because WPR is computed from LFPR and UR (WPR = LFPR x (1 - UR/100))
education figures: MoSPI's table gives no age; they match the 15 years and above figures, so they are read as that band
Across-state correlations describe states (people's chances there), not causes.
